```text
2	import type { RefObject } from 'react';

4	import type { Falsy } from '@actual-app/core/types/util';
5	
6	import {
7	  addItems,
8	  setContextMenuPosition,
9	} from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';
10	import type { ContextMenuItem } from '#contextmenu/types';
11	import { useRefEventListener } from '#hooks/useRefEventListener';
12	import { useDispatch } from '#redux';
13	
14	type UseContextMenuProps = {
15	  triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
16	  enabled?: boolean;
17	  items: Falsy<ContextMenuItem>[];
18	};
19	
20	export function useContextMenu({
21	  triggerRef,
22	  enabled = true,
23	  items,
24	}: UseContextMenuProps) {
25	  const dispatch = useDispatch();
26	
27	  // Store actions in a ref to avoid re-binding the event listener on every render
28	  const actionsRef = useRef(items);
29	  actionsRef.current = items;
30	
31	  const processedItems = items.filter(
32	    item => item && (typeof item === 'symbol' || !item.hidden),
33	  ) as ContextMenuItem[];
34	
35	  useRefEventListener(triggerRef, 'contextmenu', (e: MouseEvent) => {
36	    if (enabled) {
37	      e.preventDefault();
38	      dispatch(addItems(processedItems));
39	      dispatch(setContextMenuPosition({ x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY }));
40	    }
41	  });
42	
43	  const handleContextMenu = useCallback(() => {
44	    if (!triggerRef.current || !enabled) return;
45	    const rect = triggerRef.current.getBoundingClientRect();
46	    // prefer MouseEvent bubbling over dispatching events to
47	    // allow nesting context menu actions
48	    triggerRef.current.dispatchEvent(
49	      new MouseEvent('contextmenu', {
50	        clientX: rect.x,
51	        clientY: rect.y + rect.height,
52	        bubbles: true,
53	      }),
54	    );
55	  }, [triggerRef, enabled]);
56	
57	  return { handleContextMenu };
58	}
```

```text
3	import { Menu } from '@actual-app/components/menu';

8	import { closeContextMenu } from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';
9	import { useRefEventListener } from '#hooks/useRefEventListener';
10	import { useDispatch, useSelector } from '#redux';
11	
12	export function ContextMenu() {
13	  const dispatch = useDispatch();
14	  const { isOpen, position, items } = useSelector(state => state.contextMenu);
15	
16	  const popoverRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
17	  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
18	
19	  function handleOpenChange(newOpen: boolean) {
20	    if (!newOpen) {
21	      dispatch(closeContextMenu());
22	    }
23	  }
24	
25	  // Handle left-clicks and right-clicks to DISMISS the menu
26	  useRefEventListener(document, 'pointerdown', (e: PointerEvent) => {
27	    // Close the menu if we click anywhere outside the popover DOM element
28	    if (
29	      isOpen &&
30	      popoverRef.current &&
31	      !popoverRef.current.contains(e.target as Node)
32	    ) {
33	      handleOpenChange(false);
34	    }
35	  });
36	
37	  function handleMenuSelect(itemName: string) {
38	    for (const item of items) {
39	      if (typeof item === 'object' && item.onClick && item.name === itemName) {
40	        item.onClick();
41	        break;
42	      }
43	    }
44	    handleOpenChange(false);
45	  }
46	
47	  return (
48	    <>
49	      {/* THE INVISIBLE ANCHOR:
50	        A 0x0 pixel real DOM node that follows your right-clicks.
51	      */}
52	      <div
53	        ref={triggerRef}
54	        style={{
55	          position: 'fixed',
56	          left: position.x,
57	          top: position.y,
58	          width: 0,
59	          height: 0,
60	          pointerEvents: 'none', // Prevents it from interfering with user clicks
61	        }}
62	      />
63	      <Popover
64	        ref={popoverRef}
65	        triggerRef={triggerRef}
66	        isOpen={isOpen && !!items.length}
67	        onOpenChange={handleOpenChange}
68	        placement="bottom start"
69	        isNonModal
70	        style={{ width: 200, margin: 1 }}
71	      >
72	        <Menu
73	          onMenuSelect={handleMenuSelect}
74	          items={items as MenuItem[]}
75	          style={{ backgroundColor: theme.menuBackground }}
76	        />
77	      </Popover>
78	    </>
79	  );
80	}
```

```text
1	import { createSlice } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
2	import type { PayloadAction } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
3	
4	import type { ContextMenuItem } from './types';
5	
6	const sliceName = 'contextMenu';
7	
8	type ContextMenuState = {
9	  isOpen: boolean;
10	  position: { x: number; y: number };
11	  items: ContextMenuItem[];
12	};
13	
14	const initialState: ContextMenuState = {
15	  isOpen: false,
16	  position: { x: 0, y: 0 },
17	  items: [],
18	};
19	
20	const contextMenuSlice = createSlice({
21	  name: sliceName,
22	  initialState,
23	  reducers: {
24	    addItems(state, action: PayloadAction<ContextMenuItem[]>) {
25	      for (const item of action.payload) {
26	        if (typeof item === 'symbol' || !item.hidden) {
27	          state.items.push(item);
28	        }
29	      }
30	
31	      state.items.sort((a, b) => {
32	        const orderA = typeof a === 'object' ? (a.order ?? 0) : 0;
33	        const orderB = typeof b === 'object' ? (b.order ?? 0) : 0;
34	        return orderA - orderB;
35	      });
36	      state.isOpen = !!state.items.length;
37	    },
38	    setContextMenuPosition(
39	      state,
40	      action: PayloadAction<{
41	        x: number;
42	        y: number;
43	      }>,
44	    ) {
45	      state.position = action.payload;
46	    },
47	    closeContextMenu(state) {
48	      state.isOpen = false;
49	      state.items = [];
50	    },
51	  },
52	});
53	
54	export const { name, reducer, getInitialState } = contextMenuSlice;
55	export const { setContextMenuPosition, closeContextMenu, addItems } =
56	  contextMenuSlice.actions;
```

## Investigation Report

### 1. `packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/BudgetName.tsx`
The dropdown is **not** a locally-owned Popover — `EditableBudgetName` uses the shared `useContextMenu` hook (`packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useContextMenu.ts`), passing a `triggerRef` (the budget-name `Button`) and a list of menu `items` (rename/settings/load backup/switch file). Clicking the button calls `handleContextMenu()`, which dispatches a synthetic `contextmenu` event that the hook's listener catches and dispatches into Redux: `addItems(processedItems)` + `setContextMenuPosition(...)` (`contextMenuSlice`, state: `isOpen`, `position`, `items`). There is no local `isOpen`/`onClose` state in `BudgetName.tsx` at all — only `editing` (rename input) is local state.

### 2. Floating sidebar container: `packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.tsx` (`FloatableSidebar`)
- Floating state lives in `SidebarProvider.tsx` (`hidden`, `setHidden`, `floating`, `alwaysFloats`) via `useSidebar()`.
- `FloatableSidebar` wraps `<Sidebar/>` in a `View` with `onMouseOver` → `sidebar.setHidden(false)` and `onMouseLeave` → `useDebounceCallback(() => sidebar.setHidden(true), 350)`. When `hidden` is true, `transform: translateX(-100%)` slides the sidebar off-screen.
- Nothing here (or in `SidebarProvider`) notifies children/dropdowns that the sidebar is about to hide — `sidebar.hidden` is only consumed for the transform/box-shadow styling in `index.tsx`.
- `Sidebar.tsx` also has a separate CSS-only `.float`/`&:hover .float` opacity trick for the toggle button, unrelated to the actual hide mechanism.

### 3. No existing "close my popover when sidebar hides" pattern exists
Grepped the whole `sidebar/` directory for `Popover`, `useMenu`, `onHoverChange`, `setHidden` usage: only `index.tsx` touches `sidebar.hidden`/`setHidden`. `Account.tsx` and `BudgetName.tsx` both use `useContextMenu`, which routes through the single **global** `ContextMenu.tsx` component (mounted once in `FinancesApp.tsx`, alongside `<FloatableSidebar/>`, both siblings — line 202 and 210). That component owns `isOpen` via Redux (`state.contextMenu.isOpen`) and closes on outside `pointerdown` only:
```tsx
// ContextMenu.tsx
useRefEventListener(document, 'pointerdown', (e: PointerEvent) => {
  if (isOpen && popoverRef.current && !popoverRef.current.contains(e.target as Node)) {
    handleOpenChange(false); // dispatch(closeContextMenu())
  }
});
```
This is why the dropdown survives the sidebar hiding: it's a global, redux-driven popover anchored to a fixed-position 0×0 div, completely decoupled from the sidebar's mouseleave/hidden logic — nothing calls `closeContextMenu()` when `sidebar.setHidden(true)` fires.

### 4. `packages/component-library/src/Popover.tsx`
Wraps `react-aria-components`'s `Popover`, fully controlled: `type PopoverProps = ComponentProps<typeof ReactAriaPopover>`, and it forwards `isOpen`/`onOpenChange` straight through (`{...props}`). It's already externally force-closable — e.g. `ContextMenu.tsx` sets `isOpen={isOpen && !!items.length}` from Redux. There's also a `isNonModal` + focusout auto-close effect, but no built-in "close on ancestor hide" behavior.

**Likely fix**: in `FloatableSidebar` (or wherever `sidebar.setHidden(true)` is triggered/debounced in `index.tsx`), also `dispatch(closeContextMenu())` (import from `#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice`) — or have `SidebarProvider`'s `setHidden` trigger it via a `useEffect` watching `sidebar.hidden`.

```text
12	export function FloatableSidebar() {

14	
15	  const sidebar = useSidebar();

17	
18	  const sidebarShouldFloat = floatingSidebar || sidebar.alwaysFloats;
19	  const debouncedHideSidebar = useDebounceCallback(
20	    () => sidebar.setHidden(true),
21	    350,
22	  );

24	  return isNarrowWidth ? null : (
25	    <View
26	      onMouseOver={
27	        sidebarShouldFloat
28	          ? e => {
29	              debouncedHideSidebar.cancel();
30	              e.stopPropagation();
31	              sidebar.setHidden(false);
32	            }
33	          : undefined
34	      }
35	      onMouseLeave={
36	        sidebarShouldFloat ? () => debouncedHideSidebar() : undefined
37	      }
38	      style={{
```

```text
9	} from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';

11	import { useRefEventListener } from '#hooks/useRefEventListener';
12	import { useDispatch } from '#redux';
13	
14	type UseContextMenuProps = {
15	  triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
16	  enabled?: boolean;
17	  items: Falsy<ContextMenuItem>[];
18	};
19	
20	export function useContextMenu({
21	  triggerRef,
22	  enabled = true,
23	  items,
24	}: UseContextMenuProps) {
25	  const dispatch = useDispatch();
26	
27	  // Store actions in a ref to avoid re-binding the event listener on every render
28	  const actionsRef = useRef(items);
29	  actionsRef.current = items;
30	
31	  const processedItems = items.filter(
32	    item => item && (typeof item === 'symbol' || !item.hidden),
33	  ) as ContextMenuItem[];
34	
35	  useRefEventListener(triggerRef, 'contextmenu', (e: MouseEvent) => {
36	    if (enabled) {
37	      e.preventDefault();
38	      dispatch(addItems(processedItems));
39	      dispatch(setContextMenuPosition({ x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY }));
40	    }
41	  });
42	
43	  const handleContextMenu = useCallback(() => {
44	    if (!triggerRef.current || !enabled) return;
45	    const rect = triggerRef.current.getBoundingClientRect();
46	    // prefer MouseEvent bubbling over dispatching events to
47	    // allow nesting context menu actions
48	    triggerRef.current.dispatchEvent(
49	      new MouseEvent('contextmenu', {
50	        clientX: rect.x,
51	        clientY: rect.y + rect.height,
52	        bubbles: true,
53	      }),
54	    );
55	  }, [triggerRef, enabled]);
56	
57	  return { handleContextMenu };
58	}
```

````md
# Fix: BudgetName dropdown stays open after floating sidebar hides

## Context

`BudgetName.tsx` (in `packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/`) opens
its dropdown menu via the shared `useContextMenu` hook. That hook doesn't own
any local open/close state — it dispatches into a **global** Redux slice
(`contextMenu` in `packages/desktop-client/src/contextmenu/contextMenuSlice.ts`)
that's rendered once at the app root by `<ContextMenu />`
(`packages/desktop-client/src/components/ContextMenu.tsx`). That component only
closes itself on an outside `pointerdown`.

The floating sidebar (`FloatableSidebar` in `sidebar/index.tsx`) hides itself
independently, via `onMouseLeave` → a 350ms-debounced `sidebar.setHidden(true)`
(state owned by `SidebarProvider.tsx`, exposed through `useSidebar()`). Nothing
currently connects "sidebar became hidden" to "close any open context menu it
triggered," so when the mouse leaves, the sidebar slides away but the
BudgetName dropdown (anchored via a fixed-position 0×0 div, decoupled from the
sidebar's layout) stays on screen until a manual click dismisses it.

The goal: close the context menu automatically whenever the floating sidebar
hides, using only code inside `packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/`.

## Approach

`SidebarProvider` is the sole owner of the `hidden` state (`setHidden` is only
ever called from `FloatableSidebar`, always within this package). Add a
`useEffect` there that dispatches `closeContextMenu()` whenever `hidden`
transitions to `true`. This covers `BudgetName`'s dropdown and any other
sidebar item that uses `useContextMenu` (e.g. `Account.tsx`), without touching
`ContextMenu.tsx` or the app root.

### File to change

**`packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx`**

- Import `useEffect` from `'react'`, `useDispatch` from `'#redux'`, and
  `closeContextMenu` from `'#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice'`.
- Inside `SidebarProvider`, add:
  ```tsx
  const dispatch = useDispatch();

  useEffect(() => {
    if (hidden) {
      dispatch(closeContextMenu());
    }
  }, [hidden, dispatch]);
  ```
- No other files need to change. The file already carries `// @ts-strict-ignore`,
  so no new strict-typing concerns.

## Verification

1. `yarn typecheck` from the repo root.
2. `yarn lint:fix` (oxlint/oxfmt) to confirm formatting/import-order rules pass.
3. Manual check with `yarn start`: enable floating sidebar (Settings → floating
   sidebar, or resize below 668px so `alwaysFloats` kicks in), hover the
   sidebar into view, click the budget name to open its dropdown, then move the
   mouse away and let the sidebar slide out — confirm the dropdown now closes
   with it instead of lingering.
4. Also verify the dropdown still works normally when the sidebar is *not*
   floating (opens and closes via outside click as before, since `hidden`
   never becomes `true` in that mode).
````

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 01:00:21Z)**_

That's a portal-vs-DOM-tree issue, not a timing coincidence.

**Root cause**

`react-aria-components`' `Popover` renders its content into a portal (an overlay layer appended near `document.body`), not as a DOM child of the sidebar's `View`. Meanwhile, `FloatableSidebar`'s hide logic (`sidebar/index.tsx`) only reacts to `onMouseOver`/`onMouseLeave` on that one physical `View` element — those are ordinary DOM events, which fire based on DOM containment, not on-screen visual proximity.

So the sequence is:

1. You click the budget name button (inside the sidebar `View`) → dropdown opens.
2. You move the cursor off the button toward a menu item. The instant the cursor leaves the sidebar's DOM box, `onMouseLeave` fires → `debouncedHideSidebar()` starts its 350ms timer.
3. Because the dropdown lives in a separate portal, hovering over it does **not** touch the sidebar's `View` at all — so nothing calls `sidebar.setHidden(false)` / `debouncedHideSidebar.cancel()` again. The 350ms timer just keeps counting while you sit on "Settings" reading the options.
4. At 350ms, `hidden` flips to `true`. That's now wired (by my fix) to `dispatch(closeContextMenu())`, so the menu vanishes — even though you're still actively hovering it.

**Why "Rename budget" seems fine and "Settings" doesn't**

It's purely about travel time/dwell time, not anything special about that item. "Rename budget" is the first item, right next to the button — you typically reach it and click within well under 350ms of leaving the sidebar box, so the timer never fires before your click closes the menu anyway. "Settings" is farther down the list, so people take longer to get there and often pause to read — long enough to cross the 350ms threshold — so the menu closes out from under them.

**Why this didn't happen before my change**

The same 350ms mouseleave timer and `hidden = true` transition were already happening pre-fix — that's the original bug (sidebar itself sliding away while the menu stayed put). The dropdown just didn't care about `hidden` before, so it stayed open regardless. My fix ties the menu's lifetime directly to that same "haven't hovered the sidebar box in 350ms" signal, which is too aggressive because it doesn't account for "hovering the dropdown" as a reason to keep things open.

Want me to fix this properly — e.g. also cancel/reset the hide timer while the dropdown is open and being hovered (or only auto-close the menu on the sidebar's full hide transition once the mouse isn't over the popover either)?

No errors. Here's a summary of the fix:

**What changed** ([SidebarProvider.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx#L38-L57)):
- Added a document-level `pointerover` listener that checks whether the hovered element is inside `[data-popover]` (the attribute `Popover.tsx` already stamps on its root DOM node) — this is the only reliable way to detect "cursor is over the portal-rendered menu," since it lives outside the sidebar's own DOM subtree.
- The `closeContextMenu()` dispatch now only fires when `hidden` is `true` **and** the cursor isn't currently over a popover.

**Resulting behavior:**
- Sidebar hides while you're hovering the dropdown → menu stays open (sidebar slides away underneath it, dropdown still usable).
- Once you move off the dropdown entirely (and the sidebar is still hidden) → the menu closes right then, instead of lingering until an explicit click elsewhere.
- If you leave both the sidebar and the dropdown before the 350ms hide-timer even fires, nothing changes from before — dropdown just closes normally on outside click/selection.

Lint and typecheck both pass. Manual re-verification in the browser (hover into "Settings," confirm it now stays open, then move off and confirm it closes) is still worth doing — want me to launch the dev server and check it?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 01:18:12Z)**_

Clean. Both lint and typecheck pass.

**Summary of the change:**

- [`index.tsx`](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.tsx): `FloatableSidebar` no longer owns the hide-timer itself. Its `onMouseOver`/`onMouseLeave` now just report `setHoveringSidebar(true/false)` to the provider — the `usehooks-ts` debounce is gone.
- [`SidebarProvider.tsx`](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx): now tracks two booleans — `hoveringSidebar` (physical hover of the sidebar `View`) and `hoveringPopover` (hover of any portal-rendered dropdown, via the `[data-popover]` check from before). A single `useLayoutEffect` derives `hidden` from both combined: if either is true, show immediately; only once *both* are false does the 350ms hide-timer start. The existing `closeContextMenu()` effect is unchanged — it still only fires once `hidden` is true and the popover isn't hovered.

This fixes the race I flagged earlier with the "just close the menu" approach — deriving `hidden` from one combined effect (rather than reacting to edge-triggered transitions from two independent debounces) avoids the scenario where moving from the popover onto the sidebar would spuriously schedule a hide.

**Resulting behavior:** hovering the dropdown now keeps the sidebar itself visible too (not just the menu); the whole thing only starts its 350ms hide-countdown once you leave both the sidebar and the dropdown.

Worth manually verifying in the browser: hover sidebar → open dropdown → move to "Settings" → confirm sidebar stays put → move off both → confirm both hide together after ~350ms. Want me to launch the dev server and check it?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 01:39:01Z)**_

Cleaned up. Here's what was actually going on and what I changed:

**Root cause:** The Git-for-Windows machine-wide default is `core.autocrlf=true`, which conflicts with this repo's own `.gitattributes` (which already pins `*.ts`/`*.tsx`/`*.js`/`*.sh`/`*.snap`/`yarn.lock` to `eol=lf` and leaves everything else to `text=auto`). This left the git index's cached stat entries (recorded file sizes, from when the repo was checked out) out of sync with the real on-disk files — e.g. `README.md`'s index entry recorded 4759 bytes (a hypothetical CRLF version) while the real file was 4668 bytes (already pure LF, byte-identical to the committed blob). `git status`'s fast path trusted that stale stat entry and reported "modified" even though `git diff` correctly showed zero actual differences.

**What I did:**
1. Verified this precisely: for all 385 files `git status` flagged, computed each one's real content hash and compared it to the committed blob — **377 were byte-identical (pure stat-cache noise)**, and only **8 had genuine content differences**.
2. Set `core.autocrlf=input` **locally for this repo only** (`git config --local`, not touched globally) — this stops future checkouts/operations here from doing the LF→CRLF conversion that caused the drift, while still guarding against ever committing CRLF by accident.
3. Ran `git add --renormalize` scoped to exactly those 377 confirmed-identical files, which refreshed their stale index cache entries with no actual content change (verified `git diff --cached` is empty — nothing got staged).

**Result:** `git status` now shows exactly 8 files — my 2 intentional sidebar edits, plus 6 files (`STUDENTS.md` and 5 files under `ai-logs/`) that already had real, unrelated content changes (a markdown table reformat) sitting in your working tree before I touched anything. I left those 6 completely alone since they're someone's in-progress edits, not CRLF noise — worth checking those weren't something you expected to already be committed.

```text
14	import { closeContextMenu } from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';
15	import { useGlobalPref } from '#hooks/useGlobalPref';
16	import { useDispatch } from '#redux';
17	
18	const HOVER_HIDE_DELAY = 350;
19	
20	type SidebarContextValue = {
21	  hidden: boolean;
22	  setHidden: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
23	  setHoveringSidebar: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
24	  floating: boolean;
25	  alwaysFloats: boolean;
26	};
27	
28	const SidebarContext = createContext<SidebarContextValue>(null);
29	
30	type SidebarProviderProps = {
31	  children: ReactNode;
32	};
33	
34	export function SidebarProvider({ children }: SidebarProviderProps) {
35	  const [floatingSidebar] = useGlobalPref('floatingSidebar');
36	  const [hidden, setHidden] = useState(true);
37	  const { width } = useResponsive();
38	  const alwaysFloats = width < 668;
39	  const floating = floatingSidebar || alwaysFloats;
40	  const dispatch = useDispatch();
41	
42	  // A dropdown menu opened from the sidebar (e.g. BudgetName's) renders in a
43	  // portal, outside the sidebar's own DOM subtree, so hovering it never
44	  // triggers the sidebar's onMouseOver/onMouseLeave. Track hover of the
45	  // sidebar and of any open popover separately, then derive `hidden` from
46	  // both combined, so the sidebar (and its menu) stay visible while either
47	  // is being used, and only hide together once neither is hovered anymore.
48	  const [hoveringSidebar, setHoveringSidebar] = useState(false);
49	  const [hoveringPopover, setHoveringPopover] = useState(false);
50	
51	  useEffect(() => {
52	    function handlePointerOver(e: PointerEvent) {
53	      const target = e.target as Element | null;
54	      setHoveringPopover(!!target?.closest?.('[data-popover]'));
55	    }
56	    document.addEventListener('pointerover', handlePointerOver);
57	    return () => document.removeEventListener('pointerover', handlePointerOver);
58	  }, []);
59	
60	  useLayoutEffect(() => {
61	    if (hoveringSidebar || hoveringPopover) {
62	      setHidden(false);
63	      return;
64	    }
65	    const timeout = setTimeout(() => setHidden(true), HOVER_HIDE_DELAY);
66	    return () => clearTimeout(timeout);
67	  }, [hoveringSidebar, hoveringPopover]);
68	
69	  useEffect(() => {
70	    if (hidden && !hoveringPopover) {
71	      dispatch(closeContextMenu());
72	    }
73	  }, [hidden, hoveringPopover, dispatch]);
74	
75	  return (
76	    <SidebarContext.Provider
77	      value={{ hidden, setHidden, setHoveringSidebar, floating, alwaysFloats }}
78	    >
79	      {children}
80	    </SidebarContext.Provider>
81	  );
82	}
83	
84	export function useSidebar() {
85	  const { hidden, setHidden, setHoveringSidebar, floating, alwaysFloats } =
86	    useContext(SidebarContext);
87	
88	  return useMemo(
89	    () => ({ hidden, setHidden, setHoveringSidebar, floating, alwaysFloats }),
90	    [hidden, setHidden, setHoveringSidebar, floating, alwaysFloats],
91	  );
92	}
```

```tsx
import { act, renderHook } from '@testing-library/react';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { Mock } from 'vitest';

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';

import { closeContextMenu } from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';
import { useGlobalPref } from '#hooks/useGlobalPref';
import { useDispatch } from '#redux';

import { SidebarProvider, useSidebar } from './SidebarProvider';

vi.mock('#redux', () => ({
  useDispatch: vi.fn(),
  useSelector: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('#hooks/useGlobalPref', () => ({
  useGlobalPref: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive', () => ({
  useResponsive: vi.fn(),
}));

function dispatchPointerOver(target: Element) {
  target.dispatchEvent(new Event('pointerover', { bubbles: true }));
}

function renderSidebar() {
  return renderHook(() => useSidebar(), { wrapper: SidebarProvider });
}

describe('SidebarProvider', () => {
  let mockDispatch: Mock;

  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    vi.useFakeTimers();

    mockDispatch = vi.fn();
    (useDispatch as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue(mockDispatch);
    (useGlobalPref as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue([false, vi.fn()]);
    (useResponsive as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue({ width: 1000 });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    document.body.innerHTML = '';
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

  it('starts hidden', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();
    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(true);
  });

  it('shows the sidebar immediately while it is being hovered', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);
  });

  it('hides the sidebar 350ms after the mouse leaves it', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });
    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(false);
    });

    // Not hidden yet -- still within the debounce window.
    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);

    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(350);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(true);
  });

  it('keeps the sidebar visible while a dropdown menu opened from it is hovered', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });
    act(() => {
      // Mouse moves off the sidebar and onto its (portal-rendered) dropdown.
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(false);
    });

    const popover = document.createElement('div');
    popover.setAttribute('data-popover', '');
    document.body.appendChild(popover);

    act(() => {
      dispatchPointerOver(popover);
    });

    // Well past the normal 350ms hide delay -- should still be visible
    // because the dropdown is being hovered.
    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);
  });

  it('hides and closes the context menu once the mouse leaves the dropdown too', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });
    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(false);
    });

    const popover = document.createElement('div');
    popover.setAttribute('data-popover', '');
    document.body.appendChild(popover);

    act(() => {
      dispatchPointerOver(popover);
    });
    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);
    mockDispatch.mockClear();

    const elsewhere = document.createElement('div');
    document.body.appendChild(elsewhere);

    act(() => {
      dispatchPointerOver(elsewhere);
    });

    // Leaving the popover restarts the same hide delay.
    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);

    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(350);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(true);
    expect(mockDispatch).toHaveBeenCalledWith(closeContextMenu());
  });

  it('does not close the context menu while the dropdown is still hovered', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });
    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(false);
    });

    const popover = document.createElement('div');
    popover.setAttribute('data-popover', '');
    document.body.appendChild(popover);

    mockDispatch.mockClear();

    act(() => {
      dispatchPointerOver(popover);
    });
    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000);
    });

    expect(mockDispatch).not.toHaveBeenCalledWith(closeContextMenu());
  });
});

```

```tsx
import { fireEvent, render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { Mock } from 'vitest';

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';

import { useGlobalPref } from '#hooks/useGlobalPref';

import { FloatableSidebar } from './index';
import { useSidebar } from './SidebarProvider';

vi.mock('@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive', () => ({
  useResponsive: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('#hooks/useGlobalPref', () => ({
  useGlobalPref: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('./SidebarProvider', () => ({
  useSidebar: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('./Sidebar', () => ({
  Sidebar: () => <div data-testid="sidebar-stub" />,
}));

describe('FloatableSidebar', () => {
  let setHoveringSidebar: Mock;

  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    setHoveringSidebar = vi.fn();
    (useResponsive as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue({ isNarrowWidth: false });
  });

  function setup({
    floatingSidebar = true,
    alwaysFloats = false,
  }: { floatingSidebar?: boolean; alwaysFloats?: boolean } = {}) {
    (useGlobalPref as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue([floatingSidebar, vi.fn()]);
    (useSidebar as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue({
      hidden: false,
      setHidden: vi.fn(),
      setHoveringSidebar,
      floating: floatingSidebar || alwaysFloats,
      alwaysFloats,
    });
    return render(<FloatableSidebar />);
  }

  it('reports hovering the sidebar on mouse over when floating', () => {
    const { getByTestId } = setup({ floatingSidebar: true });

    fireEvent.mouseOver(getByTestId('sidebar-stub').parentElement as Element);

    expect(setHoveringSidebar).toHaveBeenCalledWith(true);
  });

  it('reports the sidebar as no longer hovered on mouse leave when floating', () => {
    const { getByTestId } = setup({ floatingSidebar: true });

    fireEvent.mouseLeave(getByTestId('sidebar-stub').parentElement as Element);

    expect(setHoveringSidebar).toHaveBeenCalledWith(false);
  });

  it('does not attach hover handlers when the sidebar is docked (not floating)', () => {
    const { getByTestId } = setup({
      floatingSidebar: false,
      alwaysFloats: false,
    });
    const wrapper = getByTestId('sidebar-stub').parentElement as Element;

    fireEvent.mouseOver(wrapper);
    fireEvent.mouseLeave(wrapper);

    expect(setHoveringSidebar).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});
```

```typescript
import { act, renderHook } from '@testing-library/react';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { Mock } from 'vitest';

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';

import { closeContextMenu } from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';
import { useGlobalPref } from '#hooks/useGlobalPref';
import { useDispatch } from '#redux';

import { SidebarProvider, useSidebar } from './SidebarProvider';

vi.mock('#redux', () => ({
  useDispatch: vi.fn(),
  useSelector: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('#hooks/useGlobalPref', () => ({
  useGlobalPref: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive', () => ({
  useResponsive: vi.fn(),
}));

function dispatchPointerOver(target: Element) {
  target.dispatchEvent(new Event('pointerover', { bubbles: true }));
}

function renderSidebar() {
  return renderHook(() => useSidebar(), { wrapper: SidebarProvider });
}

describe('SidebarProvider', () => {
  let mockDispatch: Mock;

  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    vi.useFakeTimers();

    mockDispatch = vi.fn();
    (useDispatch as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue(mockDispatch);
    (useGlobalPref as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue([false, vi.fn()]);
    (useResponsive as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue({ width: 1000 });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    document.body.innerHTML = '';
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

  it('starts hidden', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();
    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(true);
  });

  it('shows the sidebar immediately while it is being hovered', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);
  });

  it('hides the sidebar 350ms after the mouse leaves it', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });
    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(false);
    });

    // Not hidden yet -- still within the debounce window.
    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);

    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(350);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(true);
  });

  it('keeps the sidebar visible while a dropdown menu opened from it is hovered', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });
    act(() => {
      // Mouse moves off the sidebar and onto its (portal-rendered) dropdown.
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(false);
    });

    const popover = document.createElement('div');
    popover.setAttribute('data-popover', '');
    document.body.appendChild(popover);

    act(() => {
      dispatchPointerOver(popover);
    });

    // Well past the normal 350ms hide delay -- should still be visible
    // because the dropdown is being hovered.
    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);
  });

  it('hides and closes the context menu once the mouse leaves the dropdown too', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });
    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(false);
    });

    const popover = document.createElement('div');
    popover.setAttribute('data-popover', '');
    document.body.appendChild(popover);

    act(() => {
      dispatchPointerOver(popover);
    });
    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);
    mockDispatch.mockClear();

    const elsewhere = document.createElement('div');
    document.body.appendChild(elsewhere);

    act(() => {
      dispatchPointerOver(elsewhere);
    });

    // Leaving the popover restarts the same hide delay.
    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(false);

    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(350);
    });

    expect(result.current.hidden).toBe(true);
    expect(mockDispatch).toHaveBeenCalledWith(closeContextMenu());
  });

  it('does not close the context menu while the dropdown is still hovered', () => {
    const { result } = renderSidebar();

    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(true);
    });
    act(() => {
      result.current.setHoveringSidebar(false);
    });

    const popover = document.createElement('div');
    popover.setAttribute('data-popover', '');
    document.body.appendChild(popover);

    mockDispatch.mockClear();

    act(() => {
      dispatchPointerOver(popover);
    });
    act(() => {
      vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000);
    });

    expect(mockDispatch).not.toHaveBeenCalledWith(closeContextMenu());
  });
});
```

   - Does **not** close the context menu while the dropdown is still hovered.

2. **[index.test.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.test.tsx)** (3 tests) — covers `FloatableSidebar`'s wiring into that logic:
   - Mouse-over calls `setHoveringSidebar(true)` when floating.
   - Mouse-leave calls `setHoveringSidebar(false)` when floating.
   - No hover handlers are attached at all when docked (not floating).

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`
